segments.text: In the last year alone, scientists found more than a thousand new ocean species. It's still just the tip of the iceberg.
One turned up in Timor-Leste, in water only one to five metres deep. You don't need a submarine. You just need to look.
Another was a shark. A brand new species of ghost shark, living eight hundred metres down in Australia's Coral Sea.
Off Japan, this worm turned out to be an entirely new species, found living inside a glass sponge, seven hundred and ninety metres down.
And in a sea cave off Marseille, on one of the most-studied coastlines on Earth, a new shrimp species had been hiding the whole time.
Here's the part that actually matters. Marine biologists estimate up to ninety percent of ocean species haven't been discovered yet.
One thousand, one hundred and twenty one new species, in one year. And we've still only seen the tip of the iceberg.
